anaemia.title: Managing Iron Deficiency Anaemia
anaemia.summary: Include iron rich foods such as leafy greens, bajra, jaggery, and pulses. Pair with vitamin C sources like lemon to support absorption. Seek medical review if you feel dizzy, extremely tired, or notice swelling.
anaemia.source: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India

prenatal.title: Essential Antenatal Care
prenatal.summary: Register your pregnancy at the nearest health centre, attend all antenatal check-ups, take iron-folic acid tablets daily, and get vaccinated for tetanus. Contact a doctor immediately for heavy bleeding, severe headache, or fever.

breastfeeding.title: Breastfeeding Guidance
breastfeeding.summary: Initiate breastfeeding within one hour of birth and continue exclusively for six months. Ensure proper latch to avoid pain. Drink clean water and eat balanced meals. Seek help from a lactation counsellor or ASHA worker for difficulties.

headache.title: Headache Self-Care Tips
headache.summary: Rest in a quiet, dark room, drink water or buttermilk to stay hydrated, and avoid skipping meals. If pain is severe, associated with high fever, repeated vomiting, weakness on one side, or follows an injury, visit the nearest doctor immediately.
